rule: PASS is not release. Smoke evidence, spec acceptance, plan completion, ACTIVE_MATCH evidence and production release are separate states.

statuses.meaning: A discovery or planning artifact was produced and is coherent, but no executable product module or runtime proof exists.
A policy or governance correction passed review. It may close a policy bug but does not itself release product capability.
A specification exists without implementation, tests or ACTIVE_MATCH execution.
A specification was corrected and accepted. It is still not executable product evidence.
A smoke or compile test passed. This proves only the tested technical condition.
The artifact exists but requires human or maintainer review before promotion.
The path failed and is closed to prevent unsafe continuation.
The next path requires operator selection or explicit priority ordering.
A release candidate exists but is not bound to production authority or runtime evidence.
The module ran against ACTIVE_MATCH and produced evidence/output inside allowed boundaries. This is stronger than smoke pass but not automatically production release.
The product module is merged, tested, claim-safe, ACTIVE_MATCH validated when required, and accepted for production use.

normalization_rules.normalized_interpretation: Inspect the test context; PASS never means release by itself.

normalization_rules.input_phrase: Product Governance Runtime Pack plan produced
ACTIVE_MATCH execution produced flat phone outputs

release_blockers: missing ACTIVE_MATCH execution when runtime evidence is required
canonical event count claimed before Canonical Event Lite
tactical truth emitted before claim gate
product module exists only as Termux spec
donor code copied without HPFA adaptation
